profile.reading:
CloudHQ LC1 sits at 21955 Loudoun County Parkway, Ashburn, Virginia, one of fourteen numbered buildings on CloudHQ's LC Campus, which the company's own current campus page places directly off Loudoun County Parkway "in the heart of Ashburn," describing the site as sitting amid "the densest concentration of fiber in the world." CloudHQ states the full LC Campus totals roughly 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load across its fourteen data centers, with 756 megawatts currently available; this is a campus-wide total that CloudHQ does not break out by individual building, so it is not applied to this specific building's own capacity figure. A third-party data center aggregator separately reports 144 megawatts specifically for LC1, a figure this profile notes as unconfirmed by the operator rather than adopting as fact. CloudHQ was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who also founded QTS Realty Trust and, per CloudHQ's own materials, was the first person in the United States to obtain an IRS ruling allowing data center income to qualify for real estate investment trust tax treatment. CloudHQ is privately held through the Fateh Family Office, with regional headquarters in Washington DC, London, and Singapore, and states a company-wide net-zero emissions target by 2040, along with generator fuel supplied by HVO biodiesel "wherever it is reliably available." CloudHQ does not name a power utility for the LC Campus on its current site; Dominion Energy is the dominant electric utility across Loudoun County as a matter of public record, though this is not independently confirmed for CloudHQ specifically.

Loudoun County's Ashburn corridor is the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, hosting dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators, including Amazon Web Services, Digital Realty, NTT, Vantage, and Centersquare/Csquare facilities, within a few miles of CloudHQ's LC Campus. CloudHQ's global portfolio spans 23 campuses and more than 30 million square feet across six countries, with more than 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load already contracted company-wide, and trade press has separately reported CloudHQ planning a 4-million-square-foot expansion campus in Ashburn beyond the LC Campus's existing footprint.

reading.body:
CloudHQ's LC Campus in Ashburn totals 1,256 MW of critical IT load across fourteen buildings, with 756 MW available for new tenants. This 8.5-million-square-foot campus sits directly off Loudoun County Parkway in the heart of Ashburn, the epicenter of US data center density. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the 756 MW of available capacity represents roughly 18,900 racks, or at 8 accelerators per rack, approximately 151,000 individual GPUs or equivalent AI accelerators that could be deployed here if fully absorbed by AI workloads.

Virginia publishes capacity figures for only 23 of its 326 mapped data center facilities. The LC Campus, at 1,256 MW, would rank 24th by published capacity in the state if considered as one facility, but no operator certification is published for this individual building, only the campus aggregate. The state's 23 published facilities total 1,375 MW, meaning this single campus represents 91 percent of Virginia's disclosed capacity.

The operator's own specification page does not state which certifications this building holds, which cloud providers or AI model makers operate here, or the power and cooling infrastructure that supplies it. The address, 21955 Loudoun County Parkway, is corroborated by industry directories and navigation sources but not confirmed directly by CloudHQ.
